app.notes: Electron + React + three.js previs app (Blockout v5.1.1) run as a browser app. Setup: mise.toml pins node 22.20.0 (npm 10.9.3); `ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1 npm ci --ignore-scripts`; `npm run build` (electron-vite) produces out/renderer, which is served as is. start.sh re-runs the seed generator (.ui-capture/seed/dist/seed.mjs, bundled from seed/seed.ts by seed/build.sh with the repo's esbuild), then runs server.mjs on $PORT. Seed data is built with the app's own engine (schema factories, choreography engine, motion presets, camera-move presets, serializer) and validated with parseProject plus ShotEvaluator. On load the bridge reopens the most recent project ('Low Tide') through the app's own loadProject + store.loadFromJson path, so the app opens straight into the editor instead of the Welcome screen. Data: 5 project folders under .ui-capture/data/projects. 'Low Tide' (open by default) is a short film with 7 scenes (harbor lot night, diner dawn, alley foot chase, warehouse brawl, hospital rooftop blue hour, nightclub dance number, beach golden hour). It has about 100 entities with labelled characters (MAYA, DEX, ELI, KOVAC, ROSA...), married props, hand-blocked marks, choreographed chase/fight/dance routines and motion-preset performances; 26 shots plus 3 drafts with camera-move presets (crane, steadicam follow, orbits, drone), rigs, a Cam B bank, an alternate blocking take, mixed aspects (2.39:1 and one 9:16) and director's shot notes; and earlier export packages in exports/. The other projects are an insurance commercial, a music video with a 12-dancer routine, a generator bake-off test and a near-empty 'Untitled 3'. There are also 7 global stage presets, shown in the Library. Main areas: titlebar mode switch STAGE / SHOOT / DELIVER; left Project rail (scenes, shots, drafts) plus Library (assets, camera moves, motions, Choreographer, presets); centre three.js viewport (Shoot adds the timeline with marks); right Inspector (entity/shot/camera/scene); Deliver shows the generator profile, passes and export. The viewport needs WebGL. I could not screenshot it: headless Chrome cannot launch inside this sandbox. I verified the server endpoints, the bridge injection and the full project load/parse path. Verification: verify/panels-check.sh server-renders every panel for every scene/shot/mode/entity selection (all pass); shot.mjs is a Playwright screenshot helper that works outside the sandbox.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. - Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.
List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. # Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). A process you start in the background can't be seen or stopped from a later command, so test servers on another port than 4474 (e.g. 5474) or in the foreground under `timeout`; anything still listening on 4474 is stopped before I check.

- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4474/ (it gets PORT=4474).
